newsitem.title: USA: Emerging market debts steady in pre-holiday trade.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debts steady in pre-holiday trade.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices were mostly firmer in moderate trading before the long holiday weekend, traders said.
Monday is a public holiday in the U.S. in observance of Martin Luther King's birthday.
Argentina papers saw a good amount of turnover early in the session, with FRB ARFLC05=RR rising to 1/2 to 89-1/8.
"Argentina's global bond gave the market something to focus on," said a trader.

Argentina is offering $2 billion global bonds in five- and 20-year tranches. Market sources said the roadshow would be in London on Monday and in New York on Tuesday, with pricing expected on Wednesday.

After the good reception for Mexico's 10-year global last week and a overall positive interest rate environment, the Argentine issue now faces less uncertainty than when it was announced on January 7, an analyst said.
The latest pricing talks put the five-year spread at 300-325 basis points and 20-year at 475-500 basis points.
Brazil papers added small gains across the board, but the performance paled in comparison to its roaring stock market.
"Foreigners are pouring money into equities," said a trader. Brazil C BR8D14=RR was up 1/4 at 75-3/4 bid.
Peru when-issued papers firmed further, ending a week of uninterrrupted gains, traders said.
Peru's economy minister Jorge Camet is in Washington and market sources expected a date for the final closing of the debt restructuring to be set in February.
The Peruvian government would resume talk with the rebels on resolving the month-long hostage crisis.
"The hostage crisis is irrelevant to the Brady deal," said a trader.
Peru PDI W/I PEPDI=RR climbed 3/8 to 61.00 and Peru FLIRB W/I RUVNUSLNS=RR added 1/8 to 55-1/2.

News that President Boris Yeltsin may leave hospital next week was positive, but buying interest was light after Thursday's technical rally, another trader said, noting: "We did not see any new customer flow."
